title: How it began
hookLine: new sutras appear in the early centuries CE; scholars still debate where and how

cards: Where did it come from? Ask a historian about the Mahayana, and the honest answer starts with a shrug. New sutras appear in the early centuries of the common era.
But who first recited them, in what kind of place, among what kind of people? The record doesn't settle it. Scholars have argued about it for a long time and still do.
That might sound like a gap. Today it's the lesson: a beginning that is still debated, and how to hold a question that won't close.

teach.b: First, what the sutras themselves say. They open the old way: thus have I heard. The Buddha is teaching, a crowd is listening.
Those who keep these texts receive them as the Buddha's word, and that is how they're read in Mahayana communities today. Second, the places scholars have looked.
Some look to the forest: monks living apart, meditating hard, perhaps seeing visions, and bringing back teachings.
Some look to the stupas, the shrines where lay people came with flowers and lamps, and ask whether devotion there shaped the new movement.
Others point to ordinary monasteries of the older schools, where monks drawn to the new sutras may have kept the same rules and lived under the same roof as everyone else.

When Chinese pilgrims later traveled through India, their accounts mention followers of the great vehicle and of other schools in the same regions, sometimes in the same places. Third, a clue inside the books.
Some of the new sutras talk about themselves. The Lotus Sutra praises those who keep it, read it, recite it and copy it out.

teach.h: A BOOK THAT ASKS TO BE COPIED.
teach.b: A text that asks to be copied expects to travel. Some scholars think the books themselves were part of the answer, carried and honored like a shrine. Fourth, what a careful person does with all this: holds it open.
Several of these ideas may be partly true at once. Nobody has to choose a winner today, and Buddhists don't need the historians' answer to read a sutra.
The beginning is still debated. That's an honest place to stand.

how: Mahayana Buddhists receive the great-vehicle sutras as the Buddha's word and recite, copy and study them, while historians continue to debate where and how the texts first appeared.

games.q: you're a historian with three good theories about where the Mahayana began and no proof for any of them. what do you do?
o: pick the one you like best
games.why: several of the ideas may be partly true at once. the beginning is still debated, and that's an honest place to stand.

practice: Bring up a question in your own life that doesn't have an answer yet, something you're unsure of rather than something urgent, and say it to yourself once, plainly. Then don't answer it; let it sit there like a stone in your palm.
When the mind rushes to solve it, notice the rush, and come back to the breath.

wordCard.voice: How it began. The Mahayana sutras appear in the early centuries of the common era, and where and how they started is still debated. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: still debated. A question can stay open and still be held with care. Go gently.
